subject: Quality Assurance & Testing
title: User Acceptance Testing in Agile
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: User Acceptance Testing in Agile.

hook.text: The team demos a feature at sprint review. The stakeholder says: 'That's not what I meant at all.'

buildup.text: User acceptance testing lets actual stakeholders verify that the software meets their real-world needs.

discovery.text: In agile, UAT happens within or right after each sprint—not months later in a separate phase.

twist.text: Early UAT finds misunderstandings cheaply. Late UAT finds them when the cost of change is enormous.

climax.text: Sprint-level UAT catches a workflow misunderstanding in week one. A waterfall UAT would have found it in month six.

punchline.text: Let users accept each sprint. Not just the final product.

quiz.question: When should UAT happen in agile?
options: Within or right after each sprint
Only after all features are built
